reason: In these floras 'sub-' means 'almost' (the approximate-value pattern, as in 'suborbicular'). The quality itself is PATO quadrangular, just as 'tetragonal' was mapped in rule C311.

Most uses are relational: veins inserted at a right angle to the midrib, or a corolla tube bent at a right angle to its base. PATO right angle to needs the other part. Uses of 'apex right-angled' give an apex angle, which belongs to the measurement patterns.
This is a count of veins without a number, like '5-nerved'. The counted part is 'vein', which config/flora_counted_parts.tsv already handles through 'veined'.
This is a direct negation of PATO flattened, handled the same way as 'unlobed' (rule C239).
This joins two shape values with a hyphen and means a shape between them. The continuum pattern covers it, the same as 'linear-lanceolate'.
This says a part is missing, and the FLOPO anatomy class domatium FLOPO_0986021 already exists. It is handled the same way as 'ebracteate'.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: elliptic (PATO_0000947, synonym ellipsoid) – spherical (PATO_0001499, synonym globular))
reason: This joins two 3-D shape values with a hyphen and means a shape between them, so it is a continuum of existing PATO terms.

label: medifixed
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being attached by a point at or near its middle. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991134 dorsifixed and FLOPO:0991135 basifixed; FLOPO:0991136 versatile adds free swinging on the filament.
reason: This is a real botanical attachment term, used for anthers and for hairs attached at the middle (malpighiaceous hairs). It completes the basifixed/dorsifixed series, and no existing term means attached at the middle without the swinging that versatile requires.

Uses like 'filament expanding below' and 'corolla expanding toward the apex' mean getting wider, read the same way as 'expanded' (rule C181). Uses like 'leaves expanding' (unfolding) are a growth stage and should go to the stage context, not this rule.

This says the part has no bristles, and PO lists bristle as a synonym of trichome. On a lemma the bristles are awns, so 'lemma without bristles' should map to awn (PO_0025349) absent, as for 'awnless'.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: margin of the part + pale colour)
reason: The quality is a colour of the margin, not of the whole sepal or bract. The bearer is the margin of the part, and the value is a pale or light colour.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: beak of the part) + docs/odp/02-bounded-measurement.md (length)
reason: This is a length measured on the beak of a fruit, achene or perigynium, not a value word. The bearer is the beak as part of the named organ, and the number goes into the measurement pattern.

label: deliquescent
definition: A shedability quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's dissolving into a watery or mucilaginous fluid soon after it has served its function, instead of being shed or persisting. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991181 marcescent and PATO:0001731 deciduous (plant); the tree-branching sense (main axis lost in repeated branching) is a different quality and is not covered.
reason: In the floras it describes corollas, petals and stipules that turn to fluid, as in Commelinaceae, which is a fate of a part. Nothing in PATO or FLOPO covers this; PATO dissolved is relational.

label: serotinous
definition: A closed quality inhering in a fruit or seed cone by virtue of its remaining closed on the plant for one or more years after maturity, releasing its seeds only in response to an environmental trigger such as fire. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991176 cleistogamous; the sense 'flowering late in the season' is not covered.
reason: This is a well-defined botanical quality of cones and fruits (Pinus, Banksia) with no PATO or FLOPO term. The rare whole-plant 'flowering serotinous' use means late flowering and should be left out.
'Appendage' is a generic part that was rejected before (it needs the organ it belongs to). Several examples are also misparses, such as the banner petal's own length.

These are moss cell walls or styles that are thickened, and PATO increased thickness has 'thickened' as a synonym. The 'evenly' (as opposed to unevenly thickened walls) is lost, so a uniform-thickening value can be raised if moss floras need that contrast.
As with 'covered' (C240), the quality is whatever does the covering (hairs, scales, petiole remains), and 'sparsely' only says how much of it there is.
This means almost four-angled. Tetragonal maps to PATO quadrangular (rule C311), and 'sub-' is the approximate-value cue.

target: inconspicuous (PATO_0000464) [bearer: veins of the part, vascular bundle (PO_0005020)]
reason: The veins are not clearly visible, so the quality is PATO inconspicuous on the veins of the leaflet or valve, the same reading as 'obscure veins' (C174).

target: new: half-shape (semi- + shape of one half of the bearer, e.g. oblong (PATO_0000946))
reason: 'Semi-' describes the outline of half a structure, such as the half of a leaf or lip lobe on one side of the midrib. One rule covers semi-oblong, semi-ovate and semi-orbicular, which is better than three terms.
Perulate means a bud covered with perules, which are bud scales. PO has bud scale leaf, so this follows the pattern of 'bracteate'.
Isostylous flowers have styles of one length in the species, which is the negation of FLOPO heterostylous, handled the same way as 'indehiscent' (C363).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: stalk (PO_0025066) of the part) + docs/odp/02-bounded-measurement.md (length)
reason: This is a length measured on the stipe of a fruit, flower or perigynium. The stipe maps to PO stalk (rule C264) as part of the named organ, and the number goes into the measurement pattern.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) + black)
reason: The colour applies to the tip of the spine, bract or petal, not to the whole part. The general rule 'X-tipped' (apex + colour) covers purple-tipped and others too.
The word has unrelated meanings (margin coloured, 'edged with white'; angled, 'sharply edged'; fringed by hairs). Each must be read from the words around it, so it is not a quality by itself.
Infertile stamens, flowers and shoots cannot reproduce, which is PATO sterile.
This joins two shape values with a hyphen and means a shape between them (broadly kidney-shaped), so it is a continuum of existing PATO terms.
Squamulose means covered with small scales, mapped the same way as 'lepidote' (C235). The lichen-thallus growth form ('composed of squamules') is out of scope.
This means almost rounded and is used of apices, so it is the approximate-value cue on PATO obtuse, whose synonym is 'roundish'.
A connective or rachilla that is 'not produced' does not extend beyond the anther or the uppermost floret, which is the negation of FLOPO excurrent.
